Doctor of Philosophy (Ph.D.) in Biomedical Sciences
Innovative Research and Academic Flexibility Give You the Edge
The Ph.D. in Biomedical Sciences at Nova Southeastern University’s Dr. Kiran C. Patel
College of Allopathic Medicine offers a dynamic blend of advanced research training
and academic flexibility. Students work alongside expert faculty in state-of-the-art
laboratories and medical facilities, engaging in innovative research from the start.
With more than 70% of the curriculum dedicated to hands-on research, and three customized
pathways aligned with your academic background, you’ll gain the skills and experience
to lead in fields like biotechnology, healthcare, government, education, and clinical
research.
Menu
Request Info
Apply Now
Quick Facts
Delivery Options
Classes for the Ph.D. in Biomedical Sciences are offered on NSU's Fort Lauderdale/Davie
Campus.
Start Dates
The Ph.D. program is available to start in Summer or Fall 2025. The program can be
completed in as little as four years.
Tuition
Visit the Tuition and Fees page for more information.
Credit Hours
The program curriculum is a minimum of 60 total credits.
Ph.D. in Biomedical Sciences: Program Details
Admission Requirements
Applicants must have:
A bachelor's degree in a STEM-related field with at least 30 STEM credit hours and
a 3.0 GPA
Three letters of recommendation
A statement of purpose (1 page)
Official transcripts
TOEFL/IELTS scores (if applicable)
Interview with faculty and program director
Criminal background check and signed confidentiality agreement
GRE not required
Steps to Apply
Submit official transcripts from all institutions*
Upload statement of purpose and three letters of recommendation
Provide TOEFL/IELTS scores (if needed)
Participate in faculty/program director interviews
Complete background check and sign required agreements
Await formal admission decision
*Official transcripts sent directly from all previously attended professional and
graduate institutions
Send the official transcripts to:
Nova Southeastern University
Enrollment Processing Services
3301 College Avenue, P.O. Box 299000
Fort Lauderdale, FL 33329-9905
Curriculum
Credits Required: Minimum of 60 total credits
Core Courses (6 credits):
Fundamentals of Research (MBS 5901)
Molecular Mechanisms of Disease (PTH 5600)
Directed Research (minimum 12 credits) Dissertation Research (minimum 30 credits) Electives: Options include Bioethics, Anatomy, Biochemistry, Pharmacology, Personalized Medicine,
and more.
Pathways are available for students with:
Bachelor’s degree
Bachelor’s and Master’s degrees
M.D./Ph.D. candidates
